title: Action-value estimate by sample averaging
summary: The true value q(a) of an action is its mean reward; the sample-average method estimates it at step t by averaging the rewards actually received each time the action was chosen, Q_t(a), with a default (such as 0) before the first selection.

title: Greedy action selection
summary: Choose an action whose current estimate is largest, A_t = argmax_a Q_t(a), breaking ties arbitrarily. It exploits current knowledge and never deliberately samples actions that look worse.

title: ε-greedy action selection
summary: Act greedily most of the time, but with a small probability ε pick an action uniformly at random, regardless of the estimates. In the limit every action is tried infinitely often, so every estimate converges to its true value.

title: Incremental computation of sample averages
summary: The average of the first k rewards can be obtained from the previous average and the newest reward alone, Q_{k+1} = Q_k + (1/k)[R_k − Q_k], so memory and computation per step stay constant.

title: NewEstimate ← OldEstimate + StepSize [Target − OldEstimate]
summary: The bracketed difference is an error in the estimate; the update moves the estimate a fraction (the step size) of the way toward a possibly noisy target. This form recurs throughout the book.

title: Constant step size for nonstationary problems
summary: When the true action values drift over time, recent rewards should count more. Replacing 1/k by a constant α in (0, 1] does exactly that.

title: Exponential, recency-weighted average
summary: With a constant step size, Q_{k+1} is a weighted average of the initial estimate and all past rewards; the weight on a reward decays geometrically with how many rewards ago it arrived, and all weights sum to 1.

title: Step-size conditions for convergence
summary: A result from stochastic approximation: estimates converge with probability 1 if the step sizes sum to infinity (steps large enough to overcome initial conditions and noise) while their squares have a finite sum (steps eventually small enough). 1/k meets both; a constant α fails the second.

title: Upper-confidence-bound (UCB) action selection
summary: Prefer actions whose estimates are high or still uncertain: maximise Q_t(a) plus an uncertainty bonus c·sqrt(ln t / N_t(a)), treating untried actions as maximising. The bonus shrinks when an action is chosen and grows slowly while it is not.
